quizName:
DMV Practice Test  #24
										  					
  

30 Questions • Passing Score 24

questions.question: When turning left from a multilane, one-way street or highway, which lane should you start from?

options.text: The middle of the intersection.
The right lane.
The left lane.
Any lane.

questions.correctAnswerText: The left lane.
questions.explanation: Always start a left turn from the left lane on multilane streets and highways.

questions.question: As you approach the top of a hill, you should:

options.text: Speed up slightly.
Be ready to stop if needed.
Keep the same speed.

questions.correctAnswerText: Be ready to stop if needed.
questions.explanation: You cannot see what is on the other side of a hill or around a curve. Slow down so you can stop if a vehicle is blocked from your view. Always adjust your speed when approaching hills or curves.

questions.question: When you see a flashing yellow light at an intersection, you should:

options.text: Stop and wait for the light to change.
Make a U-turn because the intersection is closed.
Drive carefully through the intersection.
Get ready to stop; the light is about to turn red.

questions.correctAnswerText: Drive carefully through the intersection.
questions.explanation: A flashing yellow light means go slowly and look both ways before entering the intersection.

questions.question: A fully loaded tractor-trailer traveling at 55 mph may need up to ____ feet to stop completely.

options.text: 50 feet
125 feet
400 feet
750 feet

questions.correctAnswerText: 400 feet
questions.explanation: Large trucks need much more distance to stop than cars at the same speed. A fully loaded tractor-trailer needs about 400 feet to stop when traveling at 55 mph.

questions.question: The correct way to use a freeway exit ramp is to:

options.text: Slow down before you get on the exit ramp.
Slow down after you get on the exit ramp.
Keep the same speed once you are on the exit ramp.
Pass slower traffic on the exit ramp.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slow down after you get on the exit ramp.
questions.explanation: Do not slow down until you are actually on the exit ramp. Slow down once you move onto it.

questions.question: Which statement about right-of-way is true?

options.text: If two vehicles enter an intersection at the same time, the one on the left has the right-of-way.
You can turn left in front of oncoming traffic.
You can turn right in front of a pedestrian crossing.
Never demand the right-of-way.

questions.correctAnswerText: Never demand the right-of-way.
questions.explanation: Do not demand the right-of-way. Let others go first when it is safe. At four-way stops, yield to the vehicle on your right. Always yield to oncoming traffic and pedestrians when turning.

questions.question: Broken yellow lines on roads separate:

options.text: No passing zones.
Lanes of traffic moving in the same direction.
Lanes of traffic moving in opposite directions.

questions.correctAnswerText: Lanes of traffic moving in opposite directions.
questions.explanation: Yellow lines separate traffic going in opposite directions. Broken lines mean you can pass when it is safe.

questions.question: If you miss your freeway exit, you should not:

options.text: Continue to the next exit and find another route.
Go to the next exit, leave the freeway, and return to your proper exit.
Back up on the road or shoulder.

questions.correctAnswerText: Back up on the road or shoulder.
questions.explanation: Never back up on a highway or shoulder. Continue to the next exit. Backing up causes crashes because other drivers do not expect it.

questions.question: Which of these helps direct drivers into the correct lanes for turning on some highways?

options.text: Flashing red lights
Flashing yellow lights
White lines on the side of the road
White arrows painted in the lanes

questions.correctAnswerText: White arrows painted in the lanes
questions.explanation: Arrows in lanes show which direction you should go in that lane, such as straight or turning.

questions.question: Which statement is true?

options.text: Your speed affects almost everything that happens to you while driving.
Heavy traffic does not affect how fast you should drive.
You can always drive the posted speed limit.

questions.correctAnswerText: Your speed affects almost everything that happens to you while driving.
questions.explanation: Speed affects everything in your car. Follow posted speed limits. Slow down in heavy traffic and bad weather.

questions.question: You are driving too slowly if you:

options.text: Drive slower than 40 mph on any highway.
Do not pass other cars often.
Block other vehicles that are moving at normal, safe speeds.

questions.correctAnswerText: Block other vehicles that are moving at normal, safe speeds.
questions.explanation: Never drive so slowly that you block other cars or trucks moving at normal speeds.

questions.question: A broken yellow centerline means:

options.text: You cannot pass.
You can pass on the right when the road ahead is clear.
You can pass on the left when the road ahead is clear.

questions.correctAnswerText: You can pass on the left when the road ahead is clear.
questions.explanation: A broken yellow centerline on your side means you can cross it to pass other vehicles when the road ahead is clear.

questions.question: This sign means:

options.text: Stop.
No U-turn.
Yield.
Do not enter.

questions.correctAnswerText: Do not enter.
questions.explanation: This sign is placed at the start of one-way streets and ramps. It tells you not to drive in that direction.

questions.question: You are driving on a road with two or more lanes going in the same direction. You should:

options.text: Drive in any lane.
Drive in the left lane, except to pass.
Drive in the right lane, except to pass.

questions.correctAnswerText: Drive in the right lane, except to pass.
questions.explanation: On a multilane highway, drive in the right lane. Use the left lane only to pass slower vehicles.

questions.question: The most important thing about speed and curves is that you must:

options.text: Drive at the speed limit as you enter the curve, then slow down at the sharpest part.
Slow down before you enter the curve.
Speed up gently before you enter the curve.
Drive at the speed limit before, during, and after the curve.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slow down before you enter the curve.
questions.explanation: Slow down before entering a curve. Your vehicle's weight can make turning difficult if you are going too fast.

questions.question: If dust or smoke blocks your view of other vehicles, you should slow down and turn on your:

options.text: Emergency flashers.
Parking lights.
Headlights.

questions.correctAnswerText: Headlights.
questions.explanation: Turn on your headlights whenever visibility is poor. This helps other drivers see you too.

questions.question: When should you yield your right-of-way?

options.text: Often, even at controlled intersections.
Whenever it helps prevent crashes.
Never. It confuses other drivers.

questions.correctAnswerText: Whenever it helps prevent crashes.
questions.explanation: Do not assume other drivers will give you the right-of-way. Yield whenever it helps prevent crashes.

questions.question: Your stopping distance increases when stopping on:

options.text: A wet or icy road.
Paved highways.
At night.
All of the above.

questions.correctAnswerText: A wet or icy road.
questions.explanation: Stopping distance increases on wet or icy roads. It also increases on loose gravel or stones.

questions.question: When driving past a vehicle that just parked on the side of the road, you should:

options.text: Be ready for the driver to open the car door.
Speed up.
Slam on your brakes.
Assume the driver will wait for you to pass before opening the door.

questions.correctAnswerText: Be ready for the driver to open the car door.
questions.explanation: When passing a parked vehicle, be prepared for the driver to open the door. Use extra caution near parked cars.

questions.question: Pentagonal signs show:

options.text: No passing zones.
School zones.
Speed limits.
Railroad crossings.

questions.correctAnswerText: School zones.
questions.explanation: Pentagonal signs mark school zones. Watch carefully for children and pedestrians in these areas.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: Pedestrian crossing.
Side road.
Railroad ahead.

questions.correctAnswerText: Pedestrian crossing.
questions.explanation: This sign warns that pedestrians cross at this location.

questions.question: When you park uphill on a street with a curb, what should you do?

options.text: Keep the front wheel straight and set the parking brake.
Turn the front wheels away from the curb.
Turn the front wheels toward the curb.
Turn the back wheels into the curb.

questions.correctAnswerText: Turn the front wheels away from the curb.
questions.explanation: Turn your wheels away from the curb when parking uphill. If your brakes fail, your car will roll toward the curb instead of into traffic.

questions.question: At intersections with a "Yield" sign, what must you do?

options.text: Yield the right-of-way to cross traffic that is near enough to cause conflict.
Yield the right-of-way only to vehicles on your right.
Always slow down and proceed without stopping.

questions.correctAnswerText: Yield the right-of-way to cross traffic that is near enough to cause conflict.
questions.explanation: At a yield sign, slow down or stop if needed. Give the right-of-way to any vehicles that are close enough to cause a conflict.

questions.question: Your body gets rid of approximately how much alcohol per hour?

options.text: Three alcoholic drinks an hour.
One alcoholic drink an hour.
Two alcoholic drinks an hour.
None of the above.

questions.correctAnswerText: One alcoholic drink an hour.
questions.explanation: The average person processes about one alcoholic drink per hour. How impaired you become depends on many factors, such as the amount you drink, how fast you drink it, your body weight, food intake, and your overall health.

questions.question: You approach an intersection when the traffic light turns from green to solid yellow. What should you do?

options.text: Treat it like a caution sign and continue through the intersection.
Stop immediately.
Stop before entering the intersection, unless you are too close to stop safely.
Speed up to get through the intersection before the red light appears.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stop before entering the intersection, unless you are too close to stop safely.
questions.explanation: When the light turns yellow, slow down and stop before entering the intersection if you can do so safely. If you cannot stop safely, drive carefully through the intersection.

questions.question: A solid yellow arrow on a traffic signal means:

options.text: It is never used as a traffic signal.
It has the same meaning as a circular yellow light.
Drivers may turn in the direction shown by the arrow.
A green arrow is about to appear.

questions.correctAnswerText: It has the same meaning as a circular yellow light.
questions.explanation: A solid yellow arrow means the same thing as a yellow light. Slow down and prepare for a red light.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: Merge right.
Divided highway begins.
Lane ends.

questions.correctAnswerText: Lane ends.
questions.explanation: This sign tells you that this lane will end ahead. You will need to merge into another lane.

questions.question: What does this road sign mean?

options.text: When pavement is wet, reduce your speed.
The road ahead has a series of turns or curves.
Traffic increases ahead.
Steep grade ahead.

questions.correctAnswerText: When pavement is wet, reduce your speed.
questions.explanation: This sign warns that the road is slippery when wet. In wet conditions, drive slower, avoid sudden braking or turns, and keep more distance between your car and the one ahead.

questions.question: If your car starts to skid, which way should you turn the steering wheel?

options.text: Keep the front wheels straight.
In the direction you want the vehicle to go.
In the opposite direction of the skid.
In any direction. It doesn't matter.

questions.correctAnswerText: In the direction you want the vehicle to go.
questions.explanation: Turn the steering wheel in the direction you want the vehicle to go. Once the vehicle straightens out, turn the wheel back the other way.

questions.question: At an intersection with no stop line or crosswalk markings, where should you stop?

options.text: You are not required to stop.
Slow down to make sure crossing traffic is clear.
Stop where you can see at least 200 feet on either side, even if you must enter the intersecting roadway.
Stop where you can clearly see approaching traffic before entering the intersecting roadway.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stop where you can clearly see approaching traffic before entering the intersecting roadway.
questions.explanation: Stop at the point closest to the intersecting roadway where you can see approaching traffic. Do not enter the intersecting roadway to get a better view.
